729:
The following definitions shall apply in the interpretation and enforcement of this article:
Alarm user means any person, firm or corporation in or on whose building, structure, facility, equipment or premises a security alarm system is installed.
Automatic dialing device means a device which, when activated, dials a specific telephone number and transmits an emergency message or signal.
Direct signal alarm means an alarm which directly activates an outlet located within the sheriff's department, fire department, or emergency medical services facility.
False alarm means an alarm to which the sheriff's department, fire department or emergency medical services respond, but, upon arrival at the premises, discover that no exigent circumstances exist warranting emergency assistance; provided, however, an alarm activated by an attempted unauthorized or illegal entry, of which there is positive evidence, an alarm activated by a fire or conditions conducive for a fire, or an alarm activated by an alarm user under reasonable belief that emergency services were needed, shall not constitute a false alarm.
Security alarm business means any person, firm or corporation engaged in the sale, lease, installation, maintenance or repair of security alarm systems for profit; provided, however, businesses which sell security alarm components or systems are hereby excepted from this article.
Security alarm system means any mechanical, electrical or electronic device which is designed to be activated upon the detection of an entry, intrusion, fire or other emergency in or on any building, structure, facility, equipment or premises through the emission of a sound or transmission of a signal or message.
(Ord. of 5-17-94, § 1)
730:
Every person, firm or corporation engaged in the security alarm business for profit, before conducting such business, shall obtain a business license from Lamar County. A license issued under this section will only be issued to the holder of a current low voltage license issued by the State of Georgia, proof of which must be furnished to the county clerk. The fee for a license shall be fifty dollars ($50.00) per year.
(Ord. of 5-17-94, § 2)
731:
(a) No alarm user shall install, or permit to be installed, within a security alarm system, an automatic dialing device which, upon activation, directly signals the sheriff's department, fire department, or emergency medical services and transmits a pre-recorded message.
(b) Any alarm system equipped with an audible signaling device, such as a siren or horn, shall be equipped with a timer, which shall cut off or reset the system if allowed to ring unattended for more than twenty (20) minutes.
(c) No direct signal alarm system shall be connected to the sheriff's department, fire department, or emergency medical services, except for those institutional users required by law to do so. All alarm users having a direct connection on the effective date of this article shall have sixty (60) days from the effective date of this article to disconnect such systems.
(Ord. of 5-17-94, § 3)
732:
(a) All false alarms resulting in a response by the sheriff's department, fire department, or emergency medical services shall incur the following charges:
(1) For the first and second false alarm within a month, the sheriff's department shall maintain a record thereof and send a notice, upon the second occurrence, to the alarm user that false alarms will result in service charges being imposed or citations being issued.
(2) For the third and fourth false alarms within a month, a charge of twenty-five dollars ($25.00) for each such alarm shall be assessed against the alarm user.
(3) The fifth and subsequent false alarms within a month shall constitute violations of this article and are subject to the penalties set forth herein.
(b) The sheriff, in his or her sole discretion, may waive imposition of a service charge where it is shown the alarm was activated by an equipment malfunction and where the alarm user immediately placed a call to the appropriate agency seeking to cancel the alarm before the responding unit arrived, provided necessary repairs were immediately made to prevent recurrence.
(c) At the end of each month, the sheriff shall report to the county clerk the identities of those alarm system users with three (3) or more false alarms so that the county clerk may take appropriate action pursuant to this article.
(Ord. of 5-17-94, § 4)
733:
(a) Any alarm system user responsible for more than four (4) false alarms in any month shall be punished for an offense against Lamar County and, upon citation, may be tried in magistrate court. Each such false alarm shall constitute a separate offense.
(b) Any person who willfully violates this article shall be punished for an offense against Lamar County and, upon citation, may be tried in magistrate court. Each day any such willful violation continues shall constitute a separate offense.
(c) Violations may be punished by a fine up to five hundred dollars ($500.00). Actions to restrain or enjoin continuing or prospective violations of this article may be brought by the county in the superior court of Lamar County.
(Ord. of 5-17-94, § 5)
736:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
(1) Abandoned motor vehicle shall mean a vehicle which does not bear a current state license plate, unless said vehicle is stored within a completely enclosed building or it is stored on a bona fide sales lot and is in a satisfactory operating condition.
(2) Junked motor vehicle shall mean any wrecked, nonoperable, dismantled automobile, truck, trailers of any size, recreational vehicle, motor home, or other vehicle, or any parts thereof.
(3) Motor vehicle shall mean every vehicle which is self-propelled, except for those used exclusively upon stationary rails or tracks.
(4) Vehicle shall means every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a street, avenue, highway or public thoroughfare, except those used exclusively upon stationary rails or tracks. Vehicle includes cars, trucks, trailers, recreational vehicles and motor homes.
(Ord. of 7-8-03)
737:
The presence of any junked or abandoned motor vehicle on public property or any private lot, tract or parcel of land or portion thereof, occupied or unoccupied, improved or unimproved, within the county shall be deemed a public nuisance.
(Ord. of 7-8-03)
738:
It shall be unlawful for any person to cause or maintain such a public nuisance by wrecking, dismantling, partially dismantling, rendering inoperable, abandoning or discarding any motor vehicle on the real property of another or to suffer, permit or allow junked or abandoned motor vehicles to be parked, let or maintained in their own real property.
(Ord. of 7-8-03)
739:
The provisions of this article shall not apply to:
(1) Any motor vehicle in an enclosed building.
(2) Any motor vehicle on the premises of a business enterprise operated in a lawful manner when necessary to the operation of such business enterprise.
(3) Any motor vehicle on property occupied and used for repair, reconditioning and remodeling of motor vehicles in conformance with the zoning ordinance of the county.
(4) Any motor vehicle being on property by an insurance company providing insurance to cover damages to the vehicle.
(5) Any operable motor vehicle being used only for agricultural purposes.
(Ord. of 7-8-03; Ord. of 8-26-03, § 1; Ord. of 9-23-03)
740:
The provisions of this article shall be administered and enforced by the sheriff, code enforcement department or other appropriate officials who are hereby authorized to enter upon private or public property, where cause exists, to examine a junked or abandoned motor vehicle or obtain information as to the identity of a junked or abandoned motor vehicle or to remove or cause the removal of a junked or abandoned motor vehicle declared to be a nuisance pursuant to this article. When the county has contracted with any person, such person shall be authorized to enter upon private property or public property to remove or cause the removal of a junked or abandoned motor vehicle declared to be a nuisance pursuant to this article.
(Ord. of 7-8-03)
742:
Any owner of a junked or abandoned motor vehicle being dissatisfied with the decision that a junked or abandoned motor vehicle is a public nuisance shall have the right to object to such decision by filing a notice with the magistrate court within ten (10) days. Such appeal shall be heard by the magistrate judge who may affirm, amend, or reverse the order and take other action deemed appropriate. The magistrate court shall give written notice of the date, time and place of the hearing to the appellant.
(Ord. of 7-8-03)
743:
(a) Five (5) days after the action of the magistrate court authorizing the removal of a nuisance under this article following appeal, the junked or abandoned motor vehicle may be removed from the premises by the county or its authorized agent and stored at the owner's expense.
(b) Any county officer who, under this section, causes any junked or abandoned motor vehicle to be removed from the premises shall be liable for gross negligence only as provided in O.C.G.A. § 40-11-3.
(Ord. of 7-8-03)
744:
The removal of a junked or abandoned motor vehicle under this article from the premises prior to the expiration of the ten (10) days' notice shall be considered compliance with the provisions of this article and no further action shall be taken against the owner of the junked or abandoned motor vehicle or the owner or occupants of the premises. Written permission given to the sheriff, code enforcement officer or other appropriate official for the removal of the junked or abandoned motor vehicle by the owner of the same, the owner or occupant of the premises shall be considered compliant with the provisions of this article on their part and no further action shall be taken against the person giving such permission.
(Ord. of 7-8-03)
745:
(a) Any person who pleads guilty, nolo contendere, or is convicted of violating the provisions of this ordinance shall be punished as provided in section 2-1-11 or such other general law as may be enacted in the future to provide for punishment and penalties that may be imposed by the magistrate courts of this state. In addition to fine and/or jail time, the judge may impose community service and require that the defendant abate or cure the nuisance.
(b) Each and every day that any such violation exists shall be deemed a separate offense.
(c) The imposition of any sentence for any violation under this section shall not excuse the violation to continue. (Ord. of 7-8-03)

The magistrate court shall have full jurisdiction to try and dispose of all questions of nuisance affecting the public health or welfare. Any person who pleads guilty, nolo contendere or is convicted of violating the provisions of this article shall be punished as provided in section 2-1-11 or such other general law as may be enacted in the future to provide for punishment and penalties that may be imposed by the magistrate courts of the state. In addition to the fine and/or jail sentence, the judge may impose community service and require that the defendant abate or cure the nuisance.

(a) Any official or inhabitant of the county may direct a complaint of nuisance to the code enforcement officer who shall investigate and may place the complaint on the magistrate court docket for a hearing upon the basis of the investigation. The magistrate court, after a ten-day notice to the party involved, shall hold a hearing thereon and upon finding that a nuisance does exist shall issue an order to the owner, agent in control of or tenant in possession, stating that a nuisance has been found to exist and that the nuisance must be abated within so many hours or days as the court shall deem reasonable, having consideration for the nature of the nuisance and its effect on the public.
(b) Animal control officers, license and building inspectors, and the sheriff's office shall and may also receive complaints, investigate the same and place on the court docket such complaints in the same manner as the code enforcement officer.
(Ord. No. 04-02, § 1, 6-22-04)

(a) In any case where the owner, agent or tenant fails to abate the nuisance in the time specified, or where the owner, agent or tenant cannot be served with notice, or where the nature of the nuisance is such, in the opinion of the court that it must be immediately abated, the judge may issue an order to the sheriff directing the nuisance to be abated. The sheriff in such case shall keep record of the expenses and cost of abating same, and the costs shall be billed against the owner, agent or tenant for collection as for county revenues, and these shall become a lien against the property and the same shall be filed of record with the office of the clerk of superior court.

755:
There is created the position of Lamar County Code Enforcement Officer. The Code Enforcement Officer shall have only the authority and those duties granted to him by the Lamar County Board of Commissioners. The code enforcement officer shall report to the county administrator or, in his or her absence, the board of commissioners. The code enforcement officer shall have and enjoy any and all immunities as are now and hereafter granted to it or authorized by the Lamar County Code, the constitution and laws of this state.
(Ord. No. 2011-05, § 1, 10-18-11)
756:
(a) The code enforcement officer shall have the authority to enforce all provisions of the Lamar County Code of Ordinances and all applicable state codes, rules and regulations incorporated therein (hereinafter the "Code"). The code enforcement officer shall also have the authority to conduct such investigations as may be reasonably necessary to assure or compel compliance with the provisions of the Code, including accessing property and premises at reasonable times for the purpose of conducting investigations concerning matters regulated by the Code.
(b) No person shall obstruct, hamper or interfere with the code enforcement officer while in the process of executing his official duties.
(Ord. No. 2011-05, § 1, 10-18-11)
757:
(a) Duties. The duties of the code enforcement [officer] shall include, but not be limited to, the following:
(1) Enforcing the county's codes and ordinances by responding to complaints issued.
(2) Interpreting codes and ordinances for citizens.
(3) Issuing and serving warnings, notices, and citations for violations of county codes and ordinances.
(4) Conducting investigations of violations, which includes gathering evidence, interviewing witnesses, and preparing final case documentation for presentation in court.
(5) Testifying in court as an expert witness.
(6) Collecting on returned checks written to any department within Lamar County.
(7) Escorting houses that are transported through Lamar County to ensure that proper safety requirements are met.
(8) Performing related work as required.
(9) Discharging such other duties as may be required of him/her by the county administrator, chairman, and the board of commissioners.
(b) Investigations. The code enforcement officer shall promptly investigate complaints of violations of the Code and report his findings and actions to the county administrator and the board of commissioners. Wherever possible, the code enforcement officer shall use his best efforts to prevent violations or to detect and secure the correction of violations of the Code prior to taking legal action.
(c) Notice and citation. Upon his own investigation, being advised by another county department or by a citizen, or believing that a violation of any section of the Code exists, the code enforcement officer shall cause a written notice to be directed to the person or persons responsible for such violation and the owner of the property (if different), unless, in the discretion of the code enforcement officer, an emergency is deemed to exist. The notice should include the following:
(1) The person or persons responsible for the violation;
(2) The owner or occupant of the property;
(3) The address or location of the property;
(4) The nature of the violation, including the Code section(s) being violated, and applicable penalties;
(5) A course of action for curing the violation;
(6) A time frame for compliance; and
(7) A date for re-inspection for compliance.
Following the expiration of the time set forth in the notice, the code enforcement officer shall cause a re-inspection to be performed. If the violation has not been remedied, the code enforcement officer shall issue a citation to the owner of the property and/or the responsible party for prosecution in accordance with the provisions for enforcement under the applicable Code section.
(d) Stop work orders. The code enforcement officer shall order discontinuance of any unlawful use of land, buildings or structures; removal of unlawful buildings or structures, including unlawful additions, alterations, or structural modifications; discontinuance of any unlawful work being performed; and shall pursue any other action authorized by the Code or the laws of the county or state to ensure compliance with, and prevent violations of, the provisions of the Code.
(e) Should a violation of the Code exist or be discovered, the code enforcement officer may confer with the county attorney who may then, in addition to other remedies provided by law, recommend that the county institute injunction, mandamus or any appropriate action or proceeding to prevent, enjoin, abate or remove such violation. The county attorney may also assist the code enforcement officer, upon request, to ascertain the owner of property under investigation.
(f) Emergencies. If the code enforcement officer believes that an emergency exists such that imminent harm or peril to life, health, or property is likely or is authorized by the Code, the code enforcement officer shall be authorized immediately to refer these matters, without notice to the owner, to the county attorney's office for immediate action as set forth under the applicable Code section or state law.
(Ord. No. 2011-05, § 1, 10-18-11)

Commission means the Lamar County Board of Commissioners.

761:
There is hereby established a Lamar County Recreation Department, with the purpose of establishing, maintaining and managing sports and recreational programs, events and facilities for the use of all citizens of Lamar County.
(Ord. of 5-2-00, Exh. A)
762:
The recreation department shall be funded and operated by the Board of Commissioners of Lamar County, and its employees and supervisors shall serve at the will of the commission. Funding for the employees, activities, and facilities shall be as approved by the commissioners pursuant to the county budget. The commission shall be vested with the powers, duties and obligations, necessary for the establishment, maintenance and conduct of a recreation system for all citizens of Lamar County in accordance with the laws of the state.

763:
The recreation department is responsible for the care, maintenance, operation and supervision of the recreation center, pursuant to the lease between the commission and the City of Barnesville for same.

764:

If, however, the acceptance thereof for such purposes will subject the commission to additional expense for improvements, maintenance or renewal, the acceptance of any grant or device of real estate shall be subject to the approval of the commission. Money received for such purposes, unless otherwise provided by the terms of the gift or bequest, shall be deposited in the funds of the commission. The commission may also charge nominal fees for various activities which may not be included in the original budget request.

It is resolved by the board of commissioners of Butts County, Georgia, the board of commissioners of Henry County, Georgia, the board of commissioners of Lamar County, Georgia, and the board of commissioners of Spalding County, Georgia, that The Butts-Henry-Spalding County Joint Development Authority be amended to include Lamar County, Georgia, and by this amended and restated Concurrent Resolution, there is hereby continued in effect a body corporate and politic now to be known as The Butts-Henry-Lamar-Spalding County Joint Development Authority (the "Authority").

784:
Each of the boards of commissioners severally finds and declares that there is a need for a joint development authority to function in Butts, Henry, Lamar, and Spalding Counties in order to promote trade, commerce, industry, and employment opportunities; for the public good and the general welfare; and to promote the general welfare of the state and to reduce unemployment to the greatest extent possible within Butts, Henry, Lamar, and Spalding Counties.
(Res. of 10-3-95)
785:
This article is adopted pursuant to the Development Authorities Law (Chapter 62 of Title 63 of the Official Code of Georgia) as the same was amended by The General Assembly of Georgia at the 1995 Session thereof and is intended to comply therewith and shall be governed thereby for the purpose of permitting business enterprises in the four (4) counties to qualify for the tax credits given for each new full-time job created and for all other purposes permitted by said Act.

786:
(a) The authority shall be governed by a board of directors consisting of three (3) tax paying members to be appointed by the board of commissioners of Butts County, Georgia, from the members of the Butts County Industrial Development Authority, three (3) tax paying members to be appointed by the board of commissioners of Henry County, Georgia, from the members of the Henry County Development Authority, three (3) tax paying members to be appointed by the board of commissioners of Lamar County, Georgia, from the members of the Lamar County Development Authority, and three (3) tax paying members to be appointed by the board of commissioners of Spalding County, Georgia, from the members of the Griffin Spalding County Development Authority.

The members heretofore appointed by Butts County, Henry County and Spalding County shall continue to serve for the terms already appointed with their successors to be appointed for three-year terms each as present terms expire on December 31 of each year. The appointees by each county must be residents of such county, and if a director ceases to be a resident of the county from which appointed, such director shall cease to be eligible for membership and shall be replaced. In addition to the appointed members, the executive director of each of the four (4) development authorities shall serve as a nonvoting ex officio member.

787:

794:
(a) The county will not accept deeds to roads unless they comply with this section.
(b) The right-of-way shall be at least eighty (80) feet wide. The finished road shall be at least twenty-eight (28) feet wide. The paving shall be at least twenty-four (24) feet wide. There shall be shoulders on each side of the road. Each shoulder shall be at least five (5) feet wide. The completed base shall be at least six (6) inches.
(c) Cut sections shall have a front slope of three (3) to one (1), a back slope of a minimum of one (1) to one (1). The ditch shall be at least two (2) feet deep.
(d) Fill sections shall comply with the following:
(1) Sections of one (1) foot to five (5) feet require a three (3) to one (1) slope;
(2) Sections of five (5) feet or more require a two (2) to one (1) slope.
(e) The pipe cover (c.d.) shall be at least one (1) foot. All pipe shall be staked to meet slopes both in full and cut sections according to department of transportation standards.
(f) The pipe cover (s.d.) shall be at least six (6) inches before placing the base.
(g) All cross drains shall have tail ditches if required. When grading from a cut section to a fill section the water is to be diverted from the fill section. Cross drains shall have a channel excavation if required. All pipe shall have a fall.
(h) Clearing and grubbing shall meet department of transportation specifications.
(i) Grading shall meet department of transportation specifications.
(j) Drainage shall meet department of transportation specifications.
(k) The base shall be of top soil or equivalent, and shall meet department of transportation specifications Class "A" or "B". Before surface treatment the base shall have one hundred (100) percent compaction and a one and one-half-inch crown. The base shall have single surface treatment with liquid.
(l) The seal shall comply with the following:
(1) The prime shall meet all specifications of the department of transportation.
(2) Asphalt shall meet all specifications of the department of transportation.
(3) Stone #5, 7 and 89 shall be used and meet all specifications of the department of transportation.
(4) Triple surface treatment cut back asphalt shall meet all specifications and applications of the department of transportation.
(5) Stone #5, 7 and 89 shall be used and meet all specifications of the department of transportation.
(m) All side line and center line striping will be completed. The striping requirement shall be the same as the department of transportation.
(n) All shoulders and front slopes shall be grassed. Stand requirement shall be the same as the department of transportation.
(o) Loose sod shall be placed on side drain pipe in accordance with department of transportation standards and specifications.
(p) Ditch checks shall be placed to meet department of transportation standards and specifications.
(q) The streets and roads shall be inspected by a qualified person, who will give the board of commissioners a letter stating that all materials, applications, tests and requirements meet the department of transportation specifications. One (1) year of maintenance is required.

833:
(a) All persons or firms harvesting standing timber in any unincorporated area of Lamar County for delivery as pulpwood, logs, poles, posts, or wood chips to any woodyard or processing plant located inside or outside this state shall provide notice of such harvesting operations to the Lamar County Governing Authority or the designated agent thereof prior to entering onto the property if possible, but in no event later than twenty-four (24) hours after entering onto the property. Further, such persons shall give notice of cessation of cutting within twenty-four (24) hours after the job is completed.
(b) The notice of harvesting operations required by this article shall be provided for each separate tract to be harvested. Such notice shall be made in such form as prescribed by rule or regulation of the director of the Georgia Forestry Commission, and shall include the following information:
(1) A map of the area which identifies the location of the tract to be harvested and, as to those trucks which will be traveling to and from such tract for purposes of picking up and hauling loads of cut forest products, the main point of ingress to such tract from a public road and, if different, the main point of egress from such tract to a public road. If multiple points of ingress and/or ingress will be used, all such points shall be identified;
(2) A statement as to whether the timber will be removed pursuant to a lump sum sale, per unit sale, or owner harvest for purposes of ad valorem taxation under O.C.G.A. § 48-5-7.5;
(3) The name, address, and daytime telephone number of the timber seller if the harvest is pursuant to a lump sum or per unit sale or of the timber owner if the harvest is an owner harvest; and
(4) The name, business address, business telephone number, and nighttime or emergency telephone number of the person or firm harvesting such timber.
(c) Subject to the provisions of subsection (e) of this section, the notice required by this article may be submitted in person, by transmission of an electronic record via telefacsimile or e-mail, or by mail.
(d) Subject to the provisions of subsection (e) of this section, upon notification published by the Director of the Georgia Forestry Commission that a state-wide notification website or platform is available for public use, persons or firms wishing to utilize said website or platform to provide the notice required by this article may do so at their option, and Lamar County will accept notifications submitted in this manner.
(e) On and after a date specified and published by the Director of the Georgia Forestry Commission, use of the state-wide notification website or platform shall be mandatory and shall be the sole means of providing the notice required by this article; on and after said date submission of the notice by any of the means listed in subsection (c) above shall cease and will no longer be deemed acceptable or in compliance with this article.
(f) The notice required by this article shall not be or remain effective unless and until the person or firm providing such notice has delivered to the Governing Authority of Lamar County or its designated agent a valid surety bond, executed by a surety corporation authorized to transact business in this state, protecting Lamar County against any damage caused by such person or firm in the amount of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00); provided, however, that at the option of the person or firm harvesting timber a valid irrevocable letter of credit issued by a bank or savings and loan association, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 7-1-4, in the amount of five thousand dollars ($5,000.00) may be provided in lieu of a surety bond. Such bonds or letters of credit shall be subject to the conditions set forth in subsections (g) and (h) of this section. No more than one bond or letter of credit shall be required from each person or firm harvesting timber, regardless of the number of tracts harvested in the county for so long as the bond or letter of credit remains in effect. The bond or letter of credit required herein shall be valid only for the calendar year in which it was delivered.
(g) The bond or letter of credit required by subsection (f) of this section shall protect Lamar County against any damage requiring re-ditching or repair of existing ditch structures or the removal of any harvesting residue, including tree tops, debris, logs, pulpwood and other materials, placed in or around the county's rights-of-way caused by such person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The proceeds of such bond or letter of credit shall be available to reimburse the county for any cost incurred to repair such damages or remove such debris in or around the county's rights-of-way. The proceeds of such bond or letter of credit shall also be available to reimburse the county for any costs incurred to maintain or repair county roads damaged by the ingress or egress of motor vehicles engaged in the harvest operations located within five hundred (500) feet of any point of ingress or egress of the timber harvesting operation. The right of Lamar County to call such bond or letter of credit in accordance with the provisions of subsection (h) of this section shall be in addition to any other remedies available to the county at law or in equity for damage to county roads or rights-of-way.
(h) When damage results from a person or firm's harvesting activities, the governing authority of Lamar County shall make and provide a written claim to the person or firm causing the damage within thirty (30) business days after the governing authority becomes aware of the damage. Such claim may be given in person, by telefacsimile, email or mail. The claim shall describe the damage in detail and, in compliance with subsection (i)(1) of this section, give the person or firm the opportunity to repair such damage within thirty (30) days of the notification; provided, however, the county shall be authorized to repair the damage immediately if the governing authority or its designee determines the conditions present a threat to public safety, health or welfare and, upon making such repairs, shall present to the person or firm and the issuer of the applicable bond or letter of credit an itemized list of expenses incurred as a claim against the responsible party and the issuer of its bond or letter of credit. Upon the issuance of a claim as provided in this section the governing authority of Lamar County or its designee shall notify the issuer of the bond or letter of credit that a claim has been made and will be resolved or adjudicated according to the terms of this article.
(i) Within thirty (30) days of receipt of the written claim described in subsection (h), the person or firm against whom the claim is submitted may:
(1) Repair such damage at his or its own expense with the approval and supervision of the governing authority of Lamar County or its designee. When repairs are completed to the satisfaction of the governing authority or its designee, the governing authority or its designee shall provide a written notification of satisfactory completion within five (5) business days to the responsible person or firm and to the surety issuing the bond or the bank issuing the letter of credit, thereby terminating the claim.
(2) In the event of inclement weather or other factors preventing repair of the damage, request a thirty (30) day extension to repair the damage from the governing authority of Lamar County, provided that no extensions shall exceed ninety (90) days from the date the claim was tendered. Approval of any extension shall be at the discretion of the governing authority of Lamar County or its designee.
(3) Appeal the claim to the magistrate court of Lamar County. Any such appeal must name the issuer of the bond or letter of credit as a party, who shall be served with all pleadings in the action and shall have the right to appear. The magistrate court will hear evidence and arguments within thirty (30) days of the written appeal and issue a ruling within ten (10) days of such hearing. Any such appeal shall toll the thirty (30) day period, or any extension thereof, required by subsection (h) of this section. If the magistrate court rules in favor of the person or firm against whom the claim was made, the county shall have no right to recover any proceeds of the bond or letter of credit, and judgment shall be entered against the county. If the magistrate court rules in favor of the county the court shall determine the amount of damages to which the county is entitled to recover and enter judgment accordingly; the governing authority of Lamar County shall be authorized to call the bond or letter of credit and recover from the proceeds thereof an amount equal to the judgment entered by the court, up to the total amount of the bond or letter of credit. The portion of any judgment entered in favor of the county that exceeds the amount of the bond or letter of credit shall be subject to collection by any additional remedies at law or equity.
(4) In the event the person or firm against whom the claim has been submitted fails to take any of the actions allowed under subsections (i)(1), (i)(2) or (i)(3) of this section within the time required therein, such person or firm shall be deemed to have waived any and all rights to contest the call of the bond or letter of credit.
(j) If the person or firm tendering a bond or letter of credit pursuant to the requirements of this article continues its timber harvesting operation beyond the calendar year in which the bond or letter of credit was issued, the person or firm continuing the timber harvesting operation shall tender a new bond or letter of credit within five (5) business days after the first day of the new calendar year.
(k) In the event a bond or letter of credit tendered pursuant to the requirements of this article is revoked by the surety or bank, then a valid replacement bond or letter of credit must be delivered to the governing authority of Lamar County within five (5) business days after the date of revocation in order for timber harvesting operations to continue. In addition, if the person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit caused its revocation, the amount of the bond or letter of credit required shall be increased to seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500.00) after the first revocation, and ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00) after a second revocation caused by the person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The maximum amount of the bond or letter of credit shall not exceed ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00).
(l) Submission of the notice required by this article shall authorize the person or firm submitting same to undertake the timber harvesting operation described in the notice and shall remain in effect until such time as the person or firm gives notice that the harvesting operation is complete; provided, however, that any change in the facts required to be provided for purposes of such notice, including but not limited to a change in the scope or extent of the operation, must be reported to the governing authority of Lamar County within three (3) business days after such change.
(m) Any person or firm that engages in a timber harvesting operation in the unincorporated portion of Lamar County without complying with the notice requirements of this article shall be subject to a citation and trial, and upon conviction shall be fined in an amount not to exceed one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500.00) for each violation.
(n) This article applies to activities which qualify as forestry land management practices or agricultural operations under O.C.G.A. § 12-7-17(5) and (6) on land that is zoned for or used for forestry, silvicultural or agricultural purposes. It shall not authorize land disturbing activities incidental to development in conflict with the limitations set forth in O.C.G.A. § 12-7-17(6).
(o) Consistent with O.C.G.A. § 12-6-24:
(1) No fee shall be charged to provide and submit the notice required by this article; and
(2) No permit, including a driveway permit, shall be required of the person or firm engaged in a timber harvesting operation as defined by said Code section. Persons and firms providing the notice required by this article may be asked to consult with county officials responsible for roads and public works for the purpose of minimizing damage to the county's roads, rights-of-way and infrastructure, and are urged to follow recommendations from county officials. Notwithstanding the forgoing, the person or firm conducting the timber harvest operation bears ultimate responsibility for their actions, and nothing in this article shall preclude the governing authority of Lamar County from taking any and all legal action necessary to protect its property and the health, safety and welfare of its citizens.
(Ord. No. 2021-03, § 1, 4-20-21)

Incinerator means a furnace for destruction of solid waste by controlled flame combustion. An incinerator must be capable of reducing solid waste to ash.
Inert waste landfill means a facility of more than one (1) acre accepting only wastes that will not or are not likely to cause production of leachate of environmental concern. Such wastes are limited to earth and earth-like products, concrete, cured asphalt, rock, bricks, yard trimmings, stumps, limbs, and leaves. This definition excludes industrial and demolition waste not specifically listed above. This definition also excludes any site created by a person disposing of organic inert waste (e.g. stumps and other vegetative debris) originating from their own property on to land and facilities owned by said person.
Materials recovery facility means a solid waste handling facility that provides for the extraction from solid waste of recovered materials.
Municipal solid waste landfill means a disposal facility where any amount of municipal solid waste, whether or not mixed with or including commercial waste, industrial waste, nonhazardous sludges, or small quantity generator hazardous wastes, is disposed of by means of placing an approved cover thereon.
Recovered materials means those materials which have known use, reuse or recycling potential; can be feasibly used, reused or recycled; and have been diverted or removed from the solid waste stream for sale, use, reuse or recycling, whether or not requiring subsequent separation and processing.
Recovered materials processing facility means a facility engaged solely in the storage, processing, and resale or reuse of recovered materials. Such term shall not include a solid waste handling facility; provided however, any solid waste generated by such facility shall be subject to all applicable laws and regulations relating to such solid waste. A recovered materials processing facility may also be referred to as a "recycling center."
Sanitary landfill means an area of land in which solid waste is placed for permanent disposal. The term sanitary landfill shall be interpreted to include inert waste landfills, municipal solid waste landfills, and construction and demolition (C&D) landfills.
Solid waste means any garbage or refuse; sludge from a wastewater treatment plant, or air pollution control facility; and other discarded material including solid, liquid, semisolid or contained gaseous material resulting from industrial, commercial, mining and agricultural operation and from community activities, but does not include recovered materials; solid or dissolved materials in irrigation return flows or industrial discharges that are point sources subject to permit under 33 U.S.C. § 1342; or source, special nuclear or byproduct material as defined by the Federal Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended (68 Stat. 923) or hazardous materials as defined under 40 C.F.R. § 261.3. The term solid waste shall be interpreted to include bulky waste, commercial waste, construction debris, domestic waste and yard waste.
Solid waste handling facility means any facility, the primary purpose of which is the storage, collection, transportation, treatment, utilization, processing, or disposal, or any combination thereof, of solid waste. This term includes the terms inert waste landfill, municipal solid waste landfill, materials recovery facility, construction and demolition (C&D landfill), incinerator and transfer station, each as defined in this section.
Transfer station means a facility used to transfer solid waste from one transportation vehicle to another for transportation to a disposal facility or processing operation.
Yard waste means leaves, tree limbs, weeds, decomposed vegetation and other natural and biodegradable waste such as normally results from clean-up or landscaping of residential or business yards and grounds.
Zoning administrator means the person designated by the Lamar County Board of Commissioners to administer the Lamar County Zoning Ordinance and their authorized representative.

(a) Once the completed application, all fees remitted and all documentation as described in section 2-17-72 above has been submitted, the applicant shall provide the zoning administrator with written notice of same. (f) A permit shall not be denied or revoked except for due cause, being the violation of the provisions of this article, other applicable ordinances, state or federal law, or the submission of an incomplete application or an application containing false material statements.
(g) Any application denied and later resubmitted shall be deemed to have been submitted on the date of resubmission, not the date of the original submission.
(h) Permits are not transferable from one site or facility to another. 869:
(a) In addition to the requirements of this article, the zoning Ordinance, Lamar County Soil Erosion and Sedimentation Control Ordinance, joint solid waste management plan, and any other federal, state or local, ordinance, rule or regulation, all solid waste handling facilities and recovered materials processing facilities shall comply with the following requirements of this section. For the purposes of this section, the term "facility" shall mean a solid waste handling facility or a recovered materials processing facility.
(1) [Permit.] Applicant shall hold a valid permit from the Georgia Department of Natural Resources and/or U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), if applicable, to operate the facility.
(2) [Copies of permits.] The applicant shall provide the zoning administrator with a current copy of all applicable permits from the Georgia Department of Natural Resources upon application for a land disturbance permit.
(3) Ingress and egress.
a. The main entrance of the facility shall be located on a paved road with a classification of collector or arterial as shown in the street classification system map of the Lamar County Land Use Plan.
b. The board of commissioners may consider all traffic impact and transportation facilities improvement studies, including, but not limited to, studies submitted by the applicant pursuant to section 2-17-72, above, and require the applicant to construct or improve a road to accommodate the truck travel necessitated by the operations, as condition of such operation, and for the purpose of minimizing traffic impacts to residential areas.
c. The facility shall designate at least one (1) entrance-only driveway separate from at least one (1) exit-only driveway in order to mitigate traffic congestion. All other driveways shall be designed so vehicles will exit the facility in a forward direction.
d. Unless otherwise required by the traffic impact and transportation facilities improvement study, a stop sign shall be erected and maintained by the owner/operator at all egress roads from the facility.
e. Under no circumstances shall drives or access routes to or from the facility be located within three hundred (300) linear feet of any existing residential driveway or residential subdivision entrance, as measured along the right-of-way line.
f. The applicant shall construct an acceleration/deceleration lane for entry into the main entrance of the facility consistent with state and county requirements and standards and post appropriate signage.
g. Vehicles using the facility or operating within the facility shall be covered to prevent blowing of material from the vehicle.
h. All points of vehicular access to the facility shall be locked and secured after normal business hours by means of a gate or other means of security approved by the building and zoning department.
(4) Setback requirements, site barriers, and fencing.
a. No such facility shall operate within one hundred fifty (150) feet of adjoining property boundaries and public highways, except for maintenance of said one hundred fifty (150) foot set back area including the required berm, security fence, sight barrier, and animal control.
b. A sight barrier shall be provided along all property lines of the site. Sight barrier shall consist of a one-hundred-foot-wide vegetated buffer. Where natural screening conditions of at least three hundred (300) living trees per acre do not exist, the following shall be planted: evergreen trees, not more than ten (10) feet apart in staggered rows. Trees shall be at least two (2) inches in caliper, as measured at breast height, and shall be sufficiently spaced to provide an effective sight barrier when ten (10) feet in height. Trees that die shall be promptly replaced.
c. The facility is to be enclosed by an eight-foot high, chain-link security fence with three (3) strands of barbed wire, angled forty-five (45) degrees toward the outside of the premises to the top. The security fence shall be located no less than one hundred (100) feet from the property line, along the inside edge of the sight barrier.
d. A planted berm shall be located between the security fence and the facility operations to visually screen the facility operations, but no closer than twenty (20) feet and no farther than fifty (50) feet from the security fence, as measured from the base of the berm. The berm shall consist of the following: a grassed berm six (6) feet in height and planted with evergreen trees not more then ten (10) feet apart, in staggered rows on the berm. Trees shall be at least two (2) inches in caliper, as measured at breast height, and shall be sufficiently spaced to provide effective sight barriers when ten (10) feet in height. Trees that die shall be promptly replaced.
e. All entrances shall have an eight-foot-high gate, which shall be closed and locked at all times that the facility is not open.
(5) Documentation. Written logs shall be maintained of persons who deposit solid waste or recovered materials into the facility including their name, the date, make, model and license plate of the vehicle, time in and time out, and a description of the material that is being dumped.
(6) Hours of operation. Facility hours of operation shall be limited to 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday through Saturday. A sign clearly indicating the hours of operation and prohibiting dumping at all other times shall be placed in a conspicuous location at all entrances.
(7) Safety.
a. Applicant shall use extreme care and take all available precautions to insure that prohibited waste is not dumped into the facility.
b. Suitable means shall be provided at the facility to prevent and control fires. Stockpiled soil is considered to be a satisfactory fire fighting material.
(8) Siting: proximity and expansion.
a. No portion of a facility shall be located within one thousand (1,000) feet of any of the following pre-existing uses: schools, day cares, churches, hospitals, retirement homes, personal care homes, or subdivisions of record consisting of residential dwellings for which a final plat has been approved and filed with the Lamar County Superior Court Clerk. The distance shall be measured by a straight line from the property boundary of the facility to the property boundary of the aforementioned use.
b. Any new facility or expansion of an existing facility shall be located either contiguous to an existing facility, or entirely outside of a ten-mile radius of any existing facility, as measured in a straight line from the property boundaries of the existing facility.
c. No portion of a new facility or expansion of any existing facility shall be located within a one-mile radius which contains fifty (50) or more residential dwellings. The one-mile radius shall be measured in a straight line from the boundary of the property to be used for a facility. For purposes of this paragraph, a residential dwelling shall include double wide, dwelling, cluster dwelling, condominium, garden apartment, multiple-family dwelling, patio dwelling, single-family attached, single-family detached, townhouse, two-family dwelling, factory built housing, industrialized home, manufactured home (including class A, B & C), mobile home, modular homes, multisection home, prefabricated homes, sectional home and single wide; all as defined in section 203 of the Lamar County Zoning Ordinance. This paragraph does not apply, however, to a facility to be located contiguous to an existing Facility as provided under subparagraph b. above.
(9) Nuisance abatement.
a. Air pollution, noise, and vibration, and their effects upon adjacent property owners shall be minimized by the use of adequate soundproofed equipment and buildings designed to accomplish such minimization and approved by the board of commissioners, and by the proper use of berms, walls, and natural planting screens. Interior and adjoining roads used in the operations shall have their surfaces treated to minimize air pollution, noise and vibration.
b. Rodent traps shall be placed one hundred (100) yards apart around the perimeter of the facility, inside the security fence, and shall be inspected and cleaned not less than once per day.
c. Any security lighting deemed necessary by the owner/operator shall be the sodium-vapor type and shall be aligned so that no part of the illuminated field falls on adjacent property.
d. Every facility shall, at its own expense, connect to a public water supply and install at least one (1) outlet every two hundred (200) to four hundred (400) linear feet, as determined by the Lamar County Fire Chief, along the perimeter of the facility's operational area in order to ensure adequate water supply and facilities for quick delivery of water to any part of the property for the purpose of extinguishing fires. Capacity shall be such that at least fifty (50) gallons of water per minute can be applied to any fire, continuously, for at least ten (10) hours. The source of the water supply and facilities to provide for the delivery of the water shall be indicated on the plans submitted for approval to the board of commissioners.
(Ord. No. 2008-02, § 6, 7-24-08)
870:
(a) [Compliance with standards, etc.] All federal, state and local statutes, ordinances and rules and regulations, as applicable, shall be met pertaining to the operation of inert landfills, municipal solid waste landfills and construction and demolition (C&D) landfills. Moreover, operations of said landfills shall be consistent with the joint solid waste management plan for Lamar County and the City of Milner.
(b) Materials recovery facility (MRF) and recovered materials processing facility standards.
(1) All recyclable materials shall be stored in containers with no stockpiling outside the containers.
(2) Collection, storage containers, or receptacles shall not be allowed in buffer areas.
(3) The sorting, extraction and other processing of recyclable materials shall be done within a fully enclosed building.
(4) A maximum continuous sound level of sixty-five (65) dBA and a maximum peak sound level of seventy-five (75) dBA shall not be exceeded at property lines of adjacent property.
(5) Collected materials shall not be disposed on or in the property on which the materials recovery facility (MRF) or recovered materials processing facility is located. However, an MRF or recovered materials processing facility may be operated in conjunction with a sanitary landfill.
(6) The materials recovery facility or recovered materials processing facility shall be sited and operated in accordance with applicable state and federal statutes, rules and regulations as well as the joint solid waste management plan for Lamar County and the City of Milner.
(c) Transfer station standards.
(1) Solid waste brought to a transfer station shall not be disposed of on or in the property on which the transfer station is located. However, a transfer station may be operated in conjunction with a sanitary landfill or recovered materials processing facility.
(2) Transfer stations shall be sited and operated in accordance with applicable state and federal statutes, rules and regulations as well as the joint solid waste management plan for Lamar County and the City of Milner.
(d) Incinerator standards.
(1) Solid waste must be burnt for not less than thirty (30) minutes at a temperature sufficient to reduce the solid waste to ash, followed by burial in a sanitary landfill.
(2) The operator of the incinerator must date and initial time/temperature records for each batch of solid waste. Said records are to be made available upon request.
(3) An incinerator may be operated in conjunction with a sanitary landfill or recovered materials processing facility.
(4) Incinerators shall be sited and operated in accordance with applicable state and federal statutes, rules and regulations as well as the joint solid waste management plan for Lamar County and the City of Milner.
(Ord. No. 2008-02, § 6, 7-24-08)

(a) Any appeal of a decision by the building and zoning department, zoning administrator, or other county official regarding this article shall be presented in writing to the board of commissioners within fifteen (15) calendar days of the decision of said county official(s). The appeal shall set forth with particularity the specific violation(s) that occurred, reference all applicable section(s) of this article, any other county ordinance, state or federal law, regulation, etc., give the name of the alleged violator, and provide a statement of the decision being appealed as well as the remedy sought by the appellant.
(b) The county administrator shall review the written appeal and schedule a hearing at either a regular or specially called board of commissioners meeting, provided that said hearing is held no sooner than thirty (30) calendar days and no later than sixty (60) calendar days from the date of the filing of the appeal. Notice of the hearing of the appeal shall be provided in the same manner as public hearings are noticed for rezonings initiated by the county under the zoning ordinance.
(c) The board shall review the appeal on the basis of the documentation provided as part of the written appeal and any relevant evidence submitted by county staff or the applicant at the public hearing.
(d) The laws and regulations of Lamar County, the state and federal governments, and decisions made by county official(s) are presumed to be valid. It shall be the responsibility of an applicant seeking relief to assume the burden of proof and rebut the presumption by presenting clear and convincing evidence to explain how the law, regulation, action or decision is in error and how the applicant's proposed action is consistent with the provisions of this article.
(e) It is the duty of the board to review such facts and evidence in light of the provisions of this article to balance the public health, safety and general welfare against the injury to a specific applicant that would result from the strict application of this article to the property.
(f) The board may consider whether strict application of this article would create an unnecessary or undue hardship, but only if the hardship is not the result of action taken by the applicant, owner or a previous owner. Any resulting remedy proposed by the board of commissioners shall be the minimum necessary to relieve the applicant of the hardship.
(g) After reviewing an appeal filed in accordance with this article, the board may take any of the following actions:
(1) Affirm the decision below;
(2) Refer the matter back to the decision-maker for reconsideration as to any specific criteria enumerated in this article;
(3) Grant the applicant's petition;
(4) Grant the applicant's petition with conditions regarding the use of the property, or the facilities, improvements or activities thereon.
(h) Any person aggrieved by a decision of the board of commissioners pursuant to this article may appeal to the Superior Court of Lamar County by writ of certiorari as provided by law.

(a) Installation of backflow prevention device required. All customers shall have in place a backflow prevention device of the type, design, and specifications set forth in subsection (c). Purchase, installation and inspection of the backflow prevention device shall be at the expense of the customer, consumer, or developer.
(b) Designation as high-, medium-, or low-risk customer; monthly surcharge.
(1) The authority is authorized to categorize and designate customers as high-, medium-, or low-risk customers. Said designation shall be made by the backflow prevention program manager, or such other employee or representative of the authority as may be appointed from time to time, based upon his/her evaluation of the customer's property's use and potential for contamination of the public water supply.
(2) The authority is authorized to charge each high-risk customer of the system an amount not to exceed two dollars ($2.00) monthly as a surcharge to maintain and administer the cross connection and backflow prevention program.
(c) Type of backflow prevention device required; approval of devices.
(1) A backflow prevention device shall be of the following types and installed in the following manner:
a. Low- and medium-risk customers: The low- or medium-risk customer shall provide a double check valve (DCV) backflow prevention device in a size to match that of the required service meter.
i. Specifications. The DCV checks shall have replaceable seats, capture springs and the device assembly shall include a full-port ball valve on the inlet and outlet sides, with a union or swivel coupling nut between the device and each valve. Unions or swivel nuts must be integral with the device or valves. Devices shall have three (3) ball-valve test cocks in the vertical position fitted with brass or plastic threaded plugs. A fourth vertical test cock shall be provided on the upstream side of the inlet shutoff valve. All components of the assembly, including ball valve handles and assembly bolts, shall be equal in corrosion resistance to bronze or stainless steel in order to resist electrolysis. Access to both checking devices shall be by top and/or side entry for maintenance and repair of all interior parts. Valve handles, except T-type, shall turn up to close and in board (ninety (90) degrees) to open.
ii. Installation. The DCV backflow prevention device shall not be buried in earth, but models with ready access to both checks may be installed in meter boxes, pits or vaults, provided ball valve test cocks seated with threaded plugs are used. All components of a DCV installed below ground should be resistant to electrolysis. A resilient seat shutoff valve should be near the inlet and outlet side of the device, and three (3) approved test cocks provided on the device. Test cocks below ground shall be chlorinated before use.
iii. Sample approved devices:
Hersey Model # FDC/Unions
Watts Model # U-007-QT
b. High-risk customers. The high-risk customer shall install a reduced pressure zone (RPZ) backflow prevention device.
i. Specifications. The RPZ shall be of a size to match that of the required service line or meter. The RPZ assembly shall consist of a pressure differential relief valve located between two (2) positive seating check valves. The relief valve shall function automatically by sensing the pressure differential across the first check valve and discharge the backflow to atmosphere should the check valve become damaged or fouled. The relief and check valves shall have replaceable seats, and the check valves provided with captured springs. A full-port ball valve in sizes through two (2) inches, and resilient-seat OS & Y gate valve in sizes over two (2) inches shall be on the inlet and outlet sides of the device, with a union, swivel coupling nut, or flanges between the device and each valve. Unions and swivel nuts must be integral with the device or valves. The device shall be provided with three (3) ball valve test cocks and a fourth test cock shall be provided on the upstream side of the inlet shut-off valve. Sizes through two (2) inches shall have all test cocks in the vertical position. Test cocks on all assemblies shall be provided with brass or plastic threaded plugs, and relief valve vent-ports shall have suitable connections for an air gap. When a meter or other device with bronze strainer, integral or attached, is not immediately upstream of the backflow preventer, a bronze strainer shall be provided between the inlet shutoff valve and the RPZ on sizes through two (2) inches. All components of the assembly, including ball valve handles and assembly bolts shall be equal in corrosion resistance to stainless steel. Access to both checking devices shall be by top and/or side entry for maintenance and repair.
ii. Installation. The RPZ backflow prevention device shall not be buried in earth but shall be installed above ground in a structure that permits positive drainage, has freeze protection, and is located as close as practical to the outlet side of the meter. In lieu of above ground installation, the RPZ may be installed immediately inside the facility provided no intervening connections exist between the meter and the device. Where relief valve discharge could cause water damage, it shall be piped via an air gap at the relief valve vent-port to a floor drain.
iii. Sample approved devices.
Hersey Model Nos. FRP II-U; 6CM; 6CM-RPDA
Watts Model Nos. U-009-QT; 909OSY; 909DDC.
(2) All backflow prevention devices shall be approved by the American National Standards Institute, the American Society of Sanitary Engineering, the American Water Works Association, the University of Southern California Foundation for Cross Connection Control and Hydraulic Research, or the Canadian Standards Association. All shutoff valves used with backflow prevention devices shall be resilient seated.

(1) Upon application for new water service from the authority, a consumer or developer shall be categorized as a low-, medium-, or high-risk customer and shall install the designated backflow prevention device required for that category prior to receipt of water services.
(2) Existing high-risk customers shall install the designated backflow prevention device within thirty (30) days of the adoption of this section.
(3) Existing low- and medium-risk customers shall install the designated backflow prevention device within sixty (60) days of the adoption of this section.
(4) The authority is authorized to provide service for the installation of backflow prevention devices in compliance with the standards set out in subsection (c). Installation shall be at the expense of the property owner.
(e) Inspection of backflow prevention devices required, maintenance and submission of records by property owner.
(1) All backflow prevention devices shall be maintained in proper working order. Reduced pressure zone (RPZ) devices shall be tested immediately after installation and not less than annually thereafter. Double check devices (DCV) in use by low- or medium-risk customers shall be inspected and tested immediately after installation and at not less than five-year intervals following installation.
(2) The backflow prevention device shall be tested by a nationally recognized testing laboratory in accordance with the following standards:
a. Double check valve device. ASSE standard 1015, and shall bear the ASSE seal.
b. RPZ. ASSE standard 1015, and shall bear the ASSE seal.
c. [Synthetic components.] Synthetic (i.e. rubber or nylon) components within a backflow prevention device shall be replaced not less than every five (5) years.
(3) Each customer and/or owner of property which receives water services from the authority shall maintain a written record of the location, testing, and maintenance of each backflow prevention device on his/her property. Said records shall be provided to the authority upon written request by the backflow prevention program manager.
(4) High-risk customers shall submit backflow prevention device inspection and test reports annually to the backflow prevention program manager, or such other employee or representative as may be appointed by the authority from time to time, or more frequently upon written request. Said report shall be submitted within fourteen (14) days of completion of the inspection or written request.
(5) The authority is authorized to suspend water service to a customer's premises in the event backflow prevention device inspection and test reports are not provided as required.
(f) Entry upon premises for purposes of inspection. The authority shall be authorized to conduct inspections to determine compliance with this section at the discretion of the program manager, or such other employee or representative as may be appointed by the authority from time to time. Agents and employees of the authority shall be authorized to enter the premises of the customer without notice during daylight hours for the purpose of inspection and testing of the backflow prevention device.
(g) Installation of thermal expansion device. An auxiliary release valve, or expansion chamber, shall be installed where water is heated and stored in a customer's water system, or a branch of the system, which has been closed by the installation of a backflow prevention device. Said auxiliary release valve or expansion chamber shall be installed to limit thermal expansion of the heated water to not more than eighty (80) psi static (no-flow) pressure at any fixture on the system.
(h) Lawn sprinkler or irrigation systems.
(1) Lawn sprinkler or other irrigation systems, when connected to the authority's water system, shall include adequate provision for drainage and backflow prevention.
(2) Where chemicals, pesticides, fertilizer, or other additives are utilized with a sprinkler system, said system shall have an approved reduced pressure zone (RPZ) backflow prevention device.
(i) Penalties for failure to comply with section.
(1) In the event a backflow prevention device is found not to be in compliance with those standards set forth in this article, the property owner or customer shall cause said device to be repaired or replaced so as to meet the standards set forth in this section within five (5) days of written notice by the authority. In the event the backflow prevention device is not repaired or replaced within five (5) days after written notice by the authority, the authority is authorized to suspend water service to the property owner or customer's premises without further notice until such time as the device is repaired or replaced such as to be in compliance with this section.
(2) Violation of this section by a customer or property owner may be punished by a maximum fine of five hundred dollars ($500.00) per occurrence.
All existing industrial and commercial customers of the Lamar County Water and Sewer Authority shall install at their own expense a backflow prevention valve approved by the Lamar County Water and Sewer Authority and all future industrial and commercial customers of the Lamar County Water and Sewer Authority shall be required to install at their own expense a backflow prevention valve approved by the Lamar County Water and Sewer Authority prior to the commencement of service.

"If you dispute that you have violated Lamar County's Water Use Restrictions, you have the right to request a hearing (in writing), within fifteen (15) days (or next working day if the fifteenth (15 th ) day is a legal holiday or weekend) before the clerk of the Lamar County Water and Sewer Authority, or his or her designee. Your hearing will be set on the first available date after receipt of the request and you will be given at least three (3) days notice thereof. Continuances will be granted for legal cause only."

Agriculture means the raising of soil crops, poultry, and livestock in a customary manner on tracts of land at least three (3) acres in size, including all related buildings, structures, and appurtenances necessary to carry out all associated activities. Buffer means a natural or enhanced vegetated area with limited minor land disturbances, such as trails, picnic areas, and land-use practices in accordance with published best management practices such as best management practices for forestry. Corridor means all land within the buffer areas and other setback areas specified in sections 2-25-23 and 2-25-24 of this plan.
Impervious surface means a man-made structure or surface which prevents the infiltration of stormwater into the ground below the structure or surface. Perennial stream means a stream which flows throughout the whole year as indicated on a USGS quad map.
Reservoir boundary means the edge of a water supply reservoir defined by its normal pool level of six hundred fourteen and one-half (614.5) feet above mean sea level for Eady Creek Reservoir.
Utility means public or private water or sewer piping systems, water or sewer pumping stations, electric power lines, fuel pipelines, telephone lines, roads, driveways, bridges, river/lake access facilities, stormwater systems and railroads or other utilities identified by Lamar County, the City of Milner and the City of Barnesville, Georgia.

921:
(a) The zoning ordinance of Lamar County, Georgia seeks to encourage the development of desirable land use patterns within Lamar County in accordance with the Lamar County Land Use Plan. The promotion of sound land use patterns is intended to reduce or eliminate the occurrence of certain conditions which can threaten the general health, safety, and welfare of the residents of Lamar County. These regulations should serve the following purposes:
(1) Reduce the occurrence of hazardous traffic patterns and general congestion.
(2) Secure safety from fire, panic, and other dangers.
(3) Assure that adequate light and air are provided.
(4) Prevent the overcrowding of land and undue concentration of population.
(5) Facilitate the adequate provision of public utilities and facilities.
(6) Promote adequate living conditions and sustained suitability of neighborhoods.
(7) Protect property against blight and depreciation.
(8) Promote health, safety, morals, convenience, aesthetics and general welfare.
(9) Eliminate or minimize as much as possible adverse impact on adjacent properties from the development of a piece of property.
(b) Additional benefits to the public interest which can accrue from the development of sound land use patterns are as follows:
(1) Efficient development and use of community utility networks.

926:
Administrative officer: One (1) of the persons, officers, or officials, or their authorized representative, whom the Lamar County Board of Commissioners has designated as its agent(s) for the administration of these regulations. The board of commissioners may, in its discretion, designate multiple administrative officers to administer different sections of this ordinance. Agriculture: The raising of soil crops, poultry, and livestock in a customary manner on tracts of land at least five (5) acres in size, including all related buildings, structures, and appurtenances necessary to carry out all associated activities. Retail selling of products raised on the premises is permitted provided that space necessary for the parking of customers' vehicles is provided off the public right-of-way.
Agritourism or agritainment: As is defined broadly, involves any agriculturally based operation or activity that brings paying visitors to a farm, ranch or timberlands. This includes a wide variety of activities, such as, but not limited to, farm markets, roadside stands, U-Pick operations, Christmas tree farms, pumpkin patch, local products retail operations (farm produced crafts and food products), corn mazes, farm-related interpretive facilities and exhibits, agricultural educational experiences, agriculturally related events/fairs/festivals, on site farm/garden/nursery tours, walking and bicycling tours and trails, bird watching, wildlife observation, horseback trail riding, family reunion and community organizations picnic sites and garden weddings.
Airport: A transportation terminal facility where aircraft take off and land.
Airstrip, private: An area designated for the take-off and landing of private, noncommercial aircraft, with no terminal facilities and no scheduled take-offs and landings.
Alteration: Any change in the supporting members of a building, any modification or change in construction, any addition which increases the area or height, any change in use from that of one (1) district classification to another, or movement of a building from one (1) location to another.
Antenna, dish: A structure intended for receiving audio or video signals via a satellite orbiting the earth.
